lede: A large-transformer maker riding India's grid build-out, with record order inflows but a habit of missing its own targets. FY27 guidance has been cut twice in four months, operating cash flow turned negative, and growth is lagging peers while new capacity is delayed.

short_version.text: Revenue doubled in two years (₹1,291 Cr → ₹2,507 Cr), EBITDA margin rose from 10% to 15%, and the order book reached ₹6,630 Cr after a ₹1,000 Cr+ PGCIL order. Backward integration (CTC, pressboard, bushings) should add 2–3 points of margin from FY28.

FY26 revenue guidance went ₹3,500 Cr → ₹2,500–2,600 Cr; FY27 went 35–40% → 25% growth. Five-year profit of ₹591 Cr turned into only ₹111 Cr of operating cash, and FY26 cash flow was –₹105 Cr. Margin guidance changed several times on one call.

33x trailing earnings, about the same as Voltamp and Indo Tech, which are growing faster with better cash conversion. The FY29 goal of ₹7,000–8,000 Cr would make it cheap, but the track record argues for caution.

blocks.text: TARIL makes power, distribution and specialty transformers (furnace, rectifier, reactors) from 33 kV up to 1,200 kV at plants in Moraiya, Changodar and Odhav near Ahmedabad. About 55% of the order book is state and central utilities (PGCIL, GETCO, RRVPNL), 20% EPC contractors, the rest private and export customers.

items.text: Margin depends on the order vintage: orders taken 12–15 months ago at lower prices are still being executed.
Raw materials (CRGO steel, copper, bushings) are the main cost; in-house CTC, pressboard, bushings and fabrication aim to cover 80–85% of needs.
Plant utilisation drives profit: Moraiya ran at 57–65% and Changodar at 27% in Q1 FY27.
Revenue went from ₹1,158 Cr (FY22) to ₹2,507 Cr (FY26) as grid spending rose.
A QIP in FY25 cut debt/equity from 0.84x to 0.23x and funds backward integration.
Entering HVDC through a PGCIL repair order; empanelment is 15–16 months away.

blocks.title: Net profit vs operating cash flow, ₹ Cr

items.text: Five years of net profit (₹591 Cr) produced only ₹111 Cr of operating cash. In FY26 receivables rose about ₹410 Cr and inventory was built up to December 2026 to beat supply shortages.
EBITDA margin has held at 15–16% for two years; consolidated Q1 FY27 was 19.2% with subsidiaries.
Capital employed rose ₹1,162 Cr from FY24 to FY26 while after-tax operating profit rose about ₹224 Cr; much of the QIP money is still in investments and work in progress.

items.text: Promoters hold 64.4%, unchanged for a year; no pledge shown.
Institutions are leaving: domestic institutions fell from 6.0% to 1.5% and foreign from 11% to 7.8% in a year.
EY appointed for investor relations after repeated misses.
Guidance credibility: three cuts in a row, and margin guidance changed within one call (16.5–17%, 15–16%, 15–17%).
Open World Bank matter on an earlier project.
ESOP 2024 expense of ₹10.3 Cr; contingent tax liabilities ₹19.1 Cr.
Positives: no auditor change, no material related-party transactions reported.

blocks.text: The valuation is in line with smaller transformer peers, so the market is not paying extra for TARIL's scale. The base case gives low-teens yearly returns if management finally executes; the stock has fallen from ₹501 to ₹281 as guidance was cut. The key test is whether Changodar and the backward-integration plants deliver growth and cash from H2 FY27.
